page.layout: Top: two circular coin medallions side by side, each with a legend around its rim (left: POPPEA SABINA NERO. IMP. VXOR; right: STATILIA MESSALINA NERO. IMP. VXOR). Below them one column of running text in full width, two paragraphs. No marginal notes. Running head at top centre, page number at top right, signature at bottom right.

main_text.p: POPPÆA Sabina, Tito Olio Quæstorio patre nata, Neronis vxor fuit, quam duodecimo die post diuortium Octauiæ in matrimonium accepit. hanc dilexit vnicè: & tamen ipsam quoque ictu calcis occidit, quòd se ex aurigatione serò reuersum grauida & ægra conuiciis incesserat. hæc antea nupserat Rufo Crispino Equiti Romano. huic Poppeæ omnia alia fuere præter honestum animum: sermo comis, nec absurdum ingenium: modestiam præferebat, & lasciuia tamen vtebatur: famæ nunquam pepercit, maritos & adulteros non distinguens. Vide Sueto.in Nerone. hæc luxu supramodum diffluebat, autore Plin.lib.34.cap II.in hæc verba: Nostra ætate Poppæa coniux Neronis principis, delicatioribus iumentis suas soleas ex auro quoque induere solebat.

STATILIA Messalina (altera quidem à Valeria illa Messalina Claudij vxore, de qua à nobis dictum est supra) vxor quoque fuit Neronis: hac vt potiretur, virum eius Atticū Vestinum Consulem in honore ipso trucidauit. Hæc erat Statilij Tauri bis Consulis, ac triumphalis, abneptis. Taurus hic temporibus Augusti amphitheatrum Romæ extruxerat. fuit alter eiusdem nominis, huius, vt opinor, Messalinæ frater, qui ob opes & hortos egregios, quibus Agrippina inhiabat, accusatus, vim vitæ suæ attulit. Sueton.in Nerone.

page.notes: The two coin legends are printed inside the medallion engravings; the right legend is partly cut off in the scan, so MESSALINA is doubtful. Plin. citation numeral read as II. No catchword visible.
